Hookr: dense project guide for LLMs and retrieval systems

Project identity

- Name: Hookr
- Type: schema-defined WebAssembly plugin system for Go
- Primary language: Go
- Contract format: FlatBuffers
- Plugin artifact format: WebAssembly (.wasm)
- Intended users: application developers building typed plugin systems
- Host SDK target: Go
- Plugin binding targets: Go today, Rust plugin-side generation, Zig ABI binding generation, C++ plugin-side generation, AssemblyScript ABI binding generation in progress

One-sentence summary

Hookr lets a Go host define a FlatBuffers contract, generate typed Go host and
plugin APIs, build WebAssembly plugins, and load them through a runtime that
validates compatibility and supports developer tooling such as inspect, call,
bench, TUI, and live reload.

Core model

- The host application owns the FlatBuffers schema.
- Hookr owns the Wasm ABI, method dispatch, compatibility handshake, trust
  policy, generated glue, and CLI tooling.
- One rpc_service is the plugin entrypoint.
- Every other rpc_service is a host callback module.
- Plugin methods are host-to-plugin calls.
- Host module methods are plugin-to-host calls.
- Optional plugin methods use a FlatBuffers RPC attribute, default
  hookr_optional.
- Method IDs are derived from service + method identity.
- Contract identity is based on a canonical schema hash built from FlatBuffers
  reflection data, not raw source text formatting.
- Rust support is plugin-side: generated Rust bindings are intended to build
  Wasm plugins that the existing generated Go host SDK can load by ABI.
- Zig support is plugin-side: generated Zig bindings provide the ABI layer,
  method constants, schema hash, capabilities, and raw host callback transport
  helpers for Wasm plugins loaded by the Go host SDK.
- C++ support is plugin-side: generated output combines FlatBuffers C++ headers
  with a Hookr ABI header for Wasm plugins loaded by the Go host SDK.
- AssemblyScript support is plugin-side: generated output provides the ABI
  layer, method constants, schema hash, capabilities, and raw host callback
  transport helpers for Wasm plugins loaded by the Go host SDK.

Generated Go surfaces

Host SDK:

- Open(ctx, Config) (*Runtime, error)
- Runtime.Close(ctx) error
- typed plugin methods, for example Filter(ctx, *FilterRequestT)
- borrowed-view fast paths, for example FilterView(...)
- SupportsX() helpers for optional methods

Generated Config fields:

- PluginPath: plugin artifact path
- FileOptions: trust policy such as WithHash(...) or WithAllowUnsigned()
- Host: generated aggregate struct containing host callback modules
- Reload: optional live reload config
- RuntimeOptions: forwarded to the low-level runtime

Plugin PDK:

- generated Plugin interface
- RegisterPlugin / MustRegisterPlugin
- PluginContext containing one client per host callback module
- borrowed-view host callback helpers for hot paths

Host callback model

- There is no special root Host service.
- Hookr auto-discovers host callback modules from every rpc_service other than
  the configured plugin service.
- Example:

  rpc_service Plugin {
    Balance(BalanceRequest):BalanceResponse;
  }

  rpc_service Rng {
    Int(RngIntRequest):RngIntResponse;
    Float(RngFloatRequest):RngFloatResponse;
  }

- The generated host SDK exposes:

  type Host struct {
    Rng RngHost
  }

- The host passes Config.Host when opening the plugin.
- The plugin uses ctx.Rng.Int(...) and ctx.Rng.Float(...).

Runtime behavior

- Hookr loads a plugin artifact from disk through runtime/file.go.
- Trust is explicit:
  - WithHash(...) pins the expected plugin hash.
  - WithAllowUnsigned() permits local unsigned artifacts.
- On plugin startup Hookr reads handshake metadata:
  - ABI version
  - canonical schema hash
  - capabilities
  - published plugin methods
- Hookr rejects incompatible plugins before normal traffic starts.
- Runtime calls use method IDs, not string dispatch.
- Low-level host/module dispatch lives under runtime/module.

Live reload

- Generated SDKs expose ReloadConfig.
- Hookr watches PluginPath for changes.
- During reload, Hookr blocks new calls, loads and validates the replacement,
  runs the typed OnReload hook, and swaps only on success.
- If reload fails, the current runtime remains active.
- OnReload receives the typed replacement runtime so host code can re-check
  state, warm caches, or run validation before traffic resumes.
- OnReloadError receives load or swap failures.
- Live reload is intended for development workflows.
- Reload creates a fresh Wasm instance; plugin memory does not survive
  automatically.

CLI commands

- hookr gen
  - generate FlatBuffers output plus Hookr host SDK and plugin PDK glue
  - key flags: --schema, --out, --package, --plugin-service, --lang
  - --lang go emits Go host SDK and Go plugin PDK output
  - --lang rust emits Rust plugin-side bindings and a Hookr ABI shim
  - --lang zig emits Zig plugin-side ABI bindings and raw transport helpers
  - --lang cpp emits C++ FlatBuffers headers and a Hookr ABI header
  - --lang assemblyscript emits AssemblyScript plugin-side ABI bindings
  - --lang c emits C plugin-side ABI bindings and raw transport helpers
  - --lang swift emits Swift FlatBuffers files and Hookr ABI bindings
- hookr build
  - build a Wasm plugin with TinyGo
  - key flags: --plugin, --out
- hookr inspect
  - inspect schema-derived metadata and optionally a real plugin artifact
  - key flags: --schema, optional --plugin, trust flags
- hookr call
  - invoke a plugin method using JSON input/output derived from the schema
  - key flags: --schema, --plugin, --method
- hookr tui
  - interactive Bubble Tea UI for method browsing, request editing through an
    external editor, one-off calls, loop mode, and live diagnostics
- hookr bench
  - run benchmark-focused go test invocations
- hookr version
  - print the CLI version

CLI trust behavior

- inspect requires explicit trust when a plugin artifact is supplied
- call and tui always require explicit trust
- use --hash for pinned artifacts
- use --allow-unsigned for local dev builds

Developer tooling

Inspect:

- validates schema metadata
- optionally loads a plugin and compares handshake metadata
- reports schema hash, plugin hash, methods, optional support, ABI, and
  capabilities

Call:

- loads a plugin plus schema
- accepts JSON input
- converts input via FlatBuffers tooling
- invokes one plugin method
- writes JSON output to stdout
- writes progress to stderr

TUI:

- Bubble Tea UI over the same call engine
- method list, request summary, response pane, debug pane
- request editing via $VISUAL or $EDITOR
- one-off call mode
- hot loop mode with runtime-only timing
- throughput and latency stats
- hot reload on plugin file changes

Build and toolchain facts

- Go host support is the primary first-class path.
- Hookr requires Go 1.26 or higher.
- TinyGo is the build path for plugins today.
- Plugin builds require TinyGo 0.41.0 or higher.
- Rust plugin generation requires flatc; Rust toolchain compilation is a separate plugin build step.
- flatc is required for schema generation and schema-driven JSON conversion.
- VitePress is used for docs.
- semantic-release is used for GitHub releases.

Performance model

- Runtime ABI uses method IDs to avoid string dispatch.
- Generated APIs include borrowed-view fast paths to reduce allocations on
  hot loops.
- Debug tooling may be slower than the raw runtime path when JSON conversion is
  involved.
- Loop mode in the TUI measures the raw FlatBuffer/Wasm call path rather than
  shelling out to conversion tools each iteration.

First-party examples

- textfilter:
  - minimal plugin contract
  - no host callback module
  - good first example
- urlbalancer:
  - host callback module example
  - includes CLI/TUI fixtures
- tickloop:
  - hot-loop and benchmark example

Install and version commands

- Install latest CLI:
  go install github.com/mopeyjellyfish/hookr/cmd/hookr@latest
- Confirm installed version:
  hookr version

Typical end-to-end flow

1. Write contract.fbs
2. Run:
   hookr gen --schema ./contract.fbs --out ./gen --package myhookr
3. Implement plugin using generated PDK
4. Build plugin:
   hookr build --plugin ./plugin --out ./bin/plugin.wasm
5. Implement any host callback modules required by the contract
6. Open from the host with generated Open(ctx, Config)
7. Call typed plugin methods from Go
8. Use inspect, call, or tui for debugging

Task routing guidance for agents

- If the task is about schema semantics or service roles, prefer reference/contracts.
- If the task is about generated host or plugin APIs, prefer reference/generated-go-api.
- If the task is about CLI flags or command behavior, prefer reference/cli.
- If the task is about why Hookr is designed this way, prefer explanation docs.
- If the task is about implementation internals, jump to runtime/* and internal/codegen/*.
- If the task needs working examples, prefer testdata/contracts/*.
- If a page duplicates older planning material, prefer the Diataxis pages first.
